reports.title: Meta service-identity exposure amplified by excessive secret access
reports.summary: A researcher organization reports a $150,000 base award for an exposed service identity with excessive downstream integration authority.
reports.root_cause: An exposed service identity had unnecessarily broad access to secrets, with downstream integration credentials extending the potential impact into private source repositories. Apply strong service authentication, minimize identity permissions, and separate trust between integrations.
reports.impact: Researchers report potential read/write access to 507 private repositories; their write-up says they confirmed the count and did not clone or browse repository contents.
defensive_takeaways: Require authenticated, explicitly authorized access to service identities.
Constrain secret access and integration privileges to the minimum required.
Document exposure without copying private customer or source data.

reports.title: PostgreSQL text-encoding invariant failure caused memory corruption
reports.product: PostgreSQL text handling and pgcrypto extension
reports.summary: A PostgreSQL encoding-validation failure earned Team Bugz Bunnies a $30,000 individual-entry award at ZeroDay.cloud. The vendor subsequently issued CVE-2026-2006.
reports.root_cause: A trusted extension did not uphold a database-wide text-encoding invariant, while downstream text routines relied on that invariant for memory-safe length calculations. Defensive reviews should verify contracts across parser and extension boundaries.
reports.impact: Vendor confirms that an authenticated database user could reach code execution with the database operating-system account's privileges.
defensive_takeaways: Validate encoding contracts at every trusted extension boundary.
Avoid relying on unverified text invariants for memory-length calculations.
Apply supported vendor fixes and retain regression coverage.

reports.title: Gemini Enterprise connected-content trust failure allowed persistent-memory modification
reports.summary: A researcher reports a $15,000 Google bounty for a Gemini Enterprise integration issue affecting persistent assistant memory.
reports.root_cause: Content retrieved from an external collaboration system was treated as authority for a state-changing memory operation. The defensive lesson is to preserve provenance and require explicit authorization for persistent-state changes.
reports.impact: Researcher reports modification or deletion of another test account's persistent assistant memory.
defensive_takeaways: Keep retrieved content separate from authority to change persistent state.
Require independent authorization for memory changes.
Preserve connector provenance throughout downstream decisions.

reports.title: Angular automation trust and cache isolation weakness
reports.summary: A Google-rewarded report connected an adjacent CI misconfiguration with insufficient separation of automation trust, creating a potential Angular supply-chain impact.
reports.root_cause: Untrusted workflow input and shared build state crossed trust boundaries; bot-specific approval assumptions increased the potential consequence.
reports.impact: The researcher demonstrated credential exposure and modeled the remaining path to repository control without executing the final supply-chain modification. Google classified the report as a flagship supply-chain compromise.
defensive_takeaways: Separate caches and artifacts according to trust level.
Apply consistent review invalidation and least-privilege rules to automated identities.
Record which impacts were directly demonstrated versus established through design evidence.

reports.title: GitHub package-source trust allowed dependency confusion
reports.summary: A researcher reported one dependency-confusion finding affecting GitHub build and development services and a $20,000 award.
reports.root_cause: Dependency resolution crossed the intended boundary between internal Ruby packages and a public package source.
reports.impact: The researcher observed code execution across multiple service contexts. The disclosed account does not establish a broader compromise beyond those observations.
defensive_takeaways: Define explicit package sources and reserve internal namespaces where applicable.
Treat build and developer environments as separate trust zones and minimize their credentials.

reports.title: Cloud Build approval was not bound to immutable code

cwe_mappings.note: The source explicitly names a time-of-check/time-of-use vulnerability; numeric CWE mapping is editorial.

reports.summary: A Cloud Build integration report identified a mismatch between maintainer approval and the code ultimately executed; Google awarded $30,000.
reports.root_cause: The approval decision and later code-reference resolution were not bound to the same immutable version, creating a time-of-check/time-of-use flaw.
reports.impact: Unreviewed code could run with the privileges and secrets available to a build. Impact depended on the permissions of the affected pipeline.
defensive_takeaways: Bind approval decisions to immutable content identities.
Validate that the executed revision matches the authorized revision.
Limit build identity privileges and isolate untrusted contributions.
